headline: High risk of capability conflict and cascading errors: Plandex can write/modify local code while Botpress can install packages, creating unsafe shared-workspace interactions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented, so prompt injection is not provably present. However, Botpress is a chatbot/agent and Plandex reads/writes project files in a plan-local sandbox, so if outputs are manually copied or file content is treated as instructions, a limited injection path exists. The pairwise bridge is inferred, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Botpress outputs are copied into Plandex prompts or files
IF Plandex treats project-file text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Keep Botpress outputs out of Plandex prompt text
Require explicit delimiters around any copied content
Review copied snippets before pasting
Disable auto-apply for any plan that ingests chatbot text

B_data_leakage.rationale: Botpress has no documented filesystem or network egress, while Plandex reads and writes project files and can call external model providers. If both are pointed at the same workspace, source code can flow into Plandex's backend and model calls. This is a default-configuration risk for Plandex; Botpress does not add a second leak path, so the pair is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Botpress and Plandex share a workspace containing sensitive source code
IF Plandex sends file contents to a model provider during planning
mitigations: Separate Botpress and Plandex workspaces
Exclude secrets from the shared project directory
Use a local model provider for Plandex
Turn off auto-sync of generated files
Audit which files Plandex reads before each plan

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plandex can execute shell commands, write the filesystem, and modify git state; Botpress can install packages. In a shared directory, both agents can mutate the same codebase, and Plandex's per-plan shared backend increases coordination complexity. The overlap is directly supported by both profiles, and the blast radius includes corrupted or overwritten repository state.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or filesystem path
IF Botpress package installation changes the environment used by Plandex
IF Plandex auto-applies changes while another instance is active
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Disable auto-apply in Plandex
Freeze package installation during active plans
Use git branches per agent
Require manual review before any write or commit

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plandex is explicitly review-then-apply, which reduces but does not eliminate cascade risk. Botpress can generate support or task text that Plandex may ingest as plan input; if that text is treated as authoritative, errors can propagate into code changes or shell actions. The interaction is inferred from documented behaviors, not directly sandboxed.
conditions: IF Botpress-generated text is used as Plandex plan input without verification
IF Plandex auto-apply is enabled for plans derived from Botpress output
mitigations: Require human verification of Botpress-derived facts
Keep Botpress outputs as drafts only
Disable auto-apply for Botpress-originated plans
Add a checklist for factual claims before execution

E_compliance.rationale: Botpress is documented as open-source customer-support software, while Plandex is a coding tool that handles model-provider API keys and source code. No specific residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to ordinary policy gaps rather than a clear breach. The evidence is insufficient to escalate further.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into Botpress conversations and then copied into Plandex
IF organizational policy forbids source-code transmission to external model providers
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in Botpress chats
Redact secrets before sending code to Plandex
Confirm model-provider DPA coverage
Document retention settings for both tools
